recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is; restoring the original Content-Location wording or adding duplicate prose would conflict with later published FHIR-I decisions and is unnecessary for implementer understanding.
issue_request: FHIR-6998 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 FHIR-core overview request to have an update response return an HTTP Location header with the updated resource's new service location.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied by svn build@6417, represented in git as 251260b22659fe5a0501368ecb95f1d1164c9c61, which added a Content-Location header to the Developer Introduction update response example in source/overview-dev.html.
additional_context: FHIR-7924 later removed Content-Location from HTTP response guidance, FHIR-13915 clarified how specific Location should be when versioning is or is not supported, and FHIR-26358 later made Location mandatory for successful create/update outcomes including conditional update.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active Developer Introduction update response example now uses Location, and the active RESTful API update section states that successful updates and creates SHALL return a Location header with the logical id and version id, falling back to the logical URL when versions are not tracked.

related_jiras.note: Removed the Content-Location header that FHIR-6998 originally added, explaining why the current source should use Location instead.
Clarified that Location may be version-specific when supported or fall back to the logical resource URL.
Later made Location mandatory for successful create/update outcomes, including conditional update.
